title: Homo Deus
subtitle: A Brief History of Tomorrow
pitch: Having beaten much of famine, plague and war, humans may aim for immortality, happiness and godlike powers, while algorithms come to know us better than we know ourselves.

chapters.g: With famine, plague and war much reduced, Harari asks what humanity will aim for next: longer life, happiness and new powers.
Shared stories and flexible cooperation, not just brains, let humans dominate the planet.
Modern societies put human feelings and choices at the centre of meaning and authority.
A new creed treats the universe as data flows and values whatever processes data best.
If algorithms understand our wants better than we do, authority could shift from people to machines.
The risk that many people lose economic and military value as AI takes over work.

ideas: Humanity's agenda may shift to immortality, bliss and godlike power.
Humanism gave authority to human feelings.
Dataism could move authority to algorithms.
Many people could lose economic relevance.

args.a: Algorithms will soon know us better than we know ourselves.
args.c: Recommender systems are powerful but still crude, and critics say the claim treats people as more predictable than they are.
Many economists expect new kinds of work to appear, and dislike the phrase as unhelpful.

questions: Would you let an algorithm choose your partner if it was better at it?
What gives your life meaning that data cannot measure?

o: A creed that values data processing above all
quiz.w: Harari's name for an emerging worldview.

quiz.q: What three old problems does Harari say were largely tamed?
quiz.w: That frees humanity to chase new goals.
